decision.rationale: The exact head and existing CI are green, but LP1-REQ-021/LP1-AC-008 lack the required executable post-mutation transaction-failure proof, and every successful business route returns/audits a request ID different from the ID written to its request logs.

summary: PR #3 implements the full LP-01 API, persistence, contracts, readiness, and verification slice, and all existing local and exact-head CI gates pass. Approval is withheld for two concrete issues: the committed suite does not exercise the explicitly required service-owned transaction failure after mutation, and the route layer generates a second request ID that breaks response/audit-to-log correlation. The configured shutdown grace period is also not enforced, recorded as non-blocking because production deployment is outside this slice.

findings.title: Required transaction-failure rollback has no executable regression
findings.observation: LP1-REQ-021 and LP1-AC-008 require an automated simulated transaction failure that proves no partial business fact/history remains. The suite covers deterministic pre-mutation rejection and a separate contender transaction rollback, but never fails the service-owned transaction after a business mutation and before audit/idempotency completion.
findings.trigger: A future change weakens rollback or moves an Idea, audit, or idempotency terminal write outside the application transaction while the existing tests remain green.
findings.impact: The repository can claim LP-01 atomicity without executable evidence for its failure case, allowing a partial-write regression to reach merge undetected.

evidence.description: LP1-REQ-021 explicitly lists transaction failure and LP1-AC-008 requires a simulated failure with no partial facts or history.
All repository tests were audited; deterministic rejection tests stop before business mutation and the rollback-contender test expects the reviewed service call to succeed.

findings.remediation: Add a committed integration regression that injects a service-owned failure after a business mutation but before commit, then proves business facts, audit, and terminal idempotency state all rolled back and the same key can be retried after recovery.
findings.verification: The regression fails if any write escapes the transaction, passes on the current remediation head, and the full integration and acceptance suites pass.

findings.title: Business responses and audit records use a different request ID from request logs
findings.observation: Fastify creates request.id for Pino, but buildApp injects a second ID factory into all business routes. Handlers use the second value for response metadata and write context, so first-time business requests have different log and API/audit IDs.
findings.trigger: Any successful business read or first-time write, or a domain rejection returned from a business handler.
findings.impact: Callers and operators cannot use response or audit requestId values to find the corresponding incoming/completed request logs across the entire business API.

evidence.description: Fastify genReqId and Pino use request.id, while route registration supplies another idFactory.request callback used by every handler.
An injected GET /api/v1/ideas logged req_01KYT4NB3Q53WJPG30TQ3J3Y32 and returned req_01KYT4NB3TA2FM10QAJR7V9P3Y in the same 200 response.
evidence.reference: reviewer request-ID counterexample at exact head

evidence.description: The approved design defines the server-generated first-processing request ID and request-ID-based logging.

findings.remediation: Use the Fastify request-scoped ID as the authoritative first-processing ID for route responses and command context, while preserving the documented original first-processing ID on terminal idempotent replay and explicitly distinguishing any current replay-attempt ID.
findings.verification: Route tests prove initial response, audit, and incoming/completed log IDs match; a separate replay test proves the original first-processing ID is still returned.

findings.title: Shutdown grace expiry does not bound process termination
findings.observation: The grace timer only sets process.exitCode and does not abort or force-close app.close or remaining resources, so a request attached to a live handle can keep shutdown pending beyond SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS.
findings.trigger: SIGTERM or SIGINT arrives while an in-flight handler remains blocked longer than the configured grace period.
findings.impact: A restart or deployment can hang until an external supervisor force-kills the process, contrary to the approved finite-grace behavior.

evidence.description: The timeout callback logs and sets exitCode while shutdown continues to await app.close and only then pool.end.
The approved design requires a finite in-flight grace period followed by pool closure.

findings.remediation: Make grace expiry settle the shutdown path by aborting or force-closing remaining work and resources with a defined exit outcome.
findings.verification: A child-process test holds an in-flight request, sends SIGTERM, and observes listener stop plus process exit within the configured grace and a deterministic scheduling margin.

required_actions.action: Add the required post-mutation infrastructure-failure rollback regression.
Unify first-processing request identity across logs, API responses, command context, and audit while preserving replay identity semantics.

risks.description: Atomic rollback is structurally implemented but lacks the explicitly required post-mutation failure regression.
Idempotency and promotion concurrency tests pass, but the process shutdown deadline is not enforced.
risks.mitigation: Preserve the concurrency suite and resolve PRR-003 before deployment.

risks.description: Strict API contracts pass, but response/audit request identity cannot be correlated to request logs.
risks.mitigation: Resolve PRR-002 before merge and cover initial and replay identity separately.

risks.description: LP-01 is not production deployment-ready and graceful shutdown remains incomplete.
risks.mitigation: Keep the LP-05 boundary explicit and resolve PRR-003 before deployment.
